title: Critiquing AI startup websites: clarity, one CTA, and showing a feat of strength
summary: Garry Tan and YC designers critique AI startup homepages (Rosebud, MagicFlow, Reality Defender, Pump, Voiceflow). Core lessons: make it instantly clear what you do and who it's for, drive one opinionated call to action, demo the product early, and use real customer language and social proof.

principles.text: Don't be clever if clever means confusing. A homepage must say what it is and whether it's for me.
principles.quote: you don't want to be clever if clever equals confusing and that's like the first thing that people are trying to understand when they hit a website is what is this and number two being is it for me

principles.text: Be opinionated: pick one primary action, make it the high-contrast button, demote everything else to links.
principles.quote: if you really want people to try the beta make that the call to action and then make learn more instead of a button that's equal weight just make it a link and you know one of the most important things to use is contrast

principles.text: Tie the homepage to your main KPI and push secondary products to secondary pages to get users to the aha moment fast.
principles.quote: I would recommend for Rosebud to figure out what their main kpi is and what outcome they want from people that hit their website

principles.text: For AI products, show a feat of strength: a demo of magic output people have never seen before.
principles.quote: there's some sort of feet of strength that you can show it's like they skip down to the lower tiered things like the most important thing who is it who's it for

principles.text: Generic workflow tools win by focusing on specific, common use cases rather than abstract capability.
principles.quote: nobody's like man I really need workflow software instead there's a specific problem that they're looking to solve and so usually what works kind of to your point earlier is to actually focus on very specific use cases

principles.text: Write the homepage for your ICP and use the exact words existing users use to describe your product.
principles.quote: go talk to your existing users ask them how would you describe my product and then take the exact phrase that they say and just put that up at the top of your site
